text:
olivia: getting paged - multiple services throwing 502/504s in us-west-2, CloudWatch shows NATGatewayPortAllocated high for a subset of EIPs around 08:12.
ryan: looking at VPC flow logs + nat metrics. some NAT EIPs at ~95% ephemeral port allocation, others idle. probable SNAT imbalance.
infra-bot: Alert: NAT_PORT_PRESSURE us-west-2 - breach at 08:15 - nat-gw-id: nat-0abcd
samir: on a node with failures: `ss -s` shows lots of TCP in TIME-WAIT and sockets closing fast. TIME_WAIT count ~24k on one node.
samir: quick sample from `ss -tan | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head` shows same NAT ip mapped repeatedly.
jess: DNS logs from our kube-dns show a storm of lookups to `*.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` from model-fetcher pods - repeated pulls after crash loops.
dina: ALB target group churn earlier today correlates with pod restarts; terminating pods cause short-lived re-pulls and many outbound TLS handshakes.
olivia: hypothesis: sidecar + model pull code opens new TLS per fetch, no pooling, combined with DNS/eip hash sticking some client IPs to a few NAT EIPs -> per-EIP port exhaustion.
ryan: can we get a per-EIP port heatmap? CloudWatch metric `AllocatedConnectionCount` per NAT IP + `BytesOut` should show which IPs are hot.
samir: pulled the heatmap - two EIPs are at 92/96k ports used. others <10k.
jess: tactical: deploy small egress proxy DaemonSet per AZ with keepalive and connection pooling to multiplex many pod connections through fewer upstream sockets.
dina: ops note: adding NAT EIPs (more ENIs) is fastest but costs ~$0.045/hr per NAT + EIP. include in cost doc if we escalate.
oncall-ops: throttled HPA for model-fetcher from 200 -> 140 for 30m to flatten burst while we roll mitigations.
infra-bot: Change applied: HPA cap reduced by oncall-ops at 08:27
samir: canary config for nginx egress daemonset (deployed to 2 nodes): `keepalive_timeout 60s; keepalive_requests 10000; proxy_http_version 1.1;` results: observed 5.8x reduction in origin ephemeral port churn per node.
jess: rolling DNS tweak: add annotation to cached service entries to respect client side TTL and set kube-dns upstream TTL 30s for ecr hostnames to reduce fresh resolutions.
olivia: emergency sysctl discussion: `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` can be widened, and `net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout` can be lowered to reclaim ports faster. Security/infra signoff required.
security-bot: note: sysctl changes must go through compliance review. ping security if you want emergency exception.
ryan: short-term patch: proxy + DNS TTL + HPA cap; medium-term: evaluate egress mesh vs managed NAT scaling per AZ. long-term: instrument per-pod connection reuse and add model-fetcher client pooling.
dina: cost tradeoff: estimate adding 2 EIPs per AZ ~ $X/day vs maintaining daemonset infra + observability (~$Y/day). preparing short memo.
samir: monitoring: added CloudWatch alarm for per-EIP port >= 90% and PagerDuty escalation at >=95%.
oncall-ops: I'll keep an eye on it and revert HPA cap after 30m if stable. will escalate pager at breach.
jess: note for PR: update model-fetcher to use HTTP/2 where feasible and enable persistent connections to the ecr registry.
olivia: any objections to full daemonset rollout in us-west-2 after canary? :thumbsup: to proceed if metrics hold.
ryan: :thumbsup:
jess: :thumbsup:
samir: pushing to 20% of nodes now, will report heatmap in 15m.
olivia: thanks all. follow-up: add a ticket to evaluate per-AZ NAT autoscaling + allocation strategy to avoid hash-hot spots and consider using AWS NAT Gateway Multi-IP per ENI routing to spread SNAT. leaving thread open for updates.
